name: domain-persistence
title: Establish Domain Persistence (defense-in-depth)
description: Once you own the domain (a krbtgt hash, a replicated NTDS dump, or Domain-Admin rights), lay down SEVERAL INDEPENDENT persistence mechanisms so cleaning up any one does not evict you. Each step is a separate fact-gated pack action producing its own persistence.domain fact and runs through the same scope-enforced runner as `obol run`; unmet steps (e.g. no krbtgt hash yet) are skipped, and every step is approval-gated because it modifies domain infrastructure — obol crafts and runs on approval, never silently. Post-exploitation / OSEP-tier: opt in deliberately (never needed to pass an OSCP exam).

steps.label: Golden ticket (forge a TGT from the krbtgt key)
steps.note: The krbtgt-key forgery — any user, any group, offline. The broadest persistence; survives every password reset except krbtgt (twice).

steps.label: Diamond ticket (re-sign a real DC-issued TGT)
steps.note: Stealthier than golden — modifies a legitimately-issued ticket rather than forging one, so it blends with real Kerberos traffic. Independent of the golden path above.

steps.label: WSUS abuse (push a signed update as SYSTEM)
steps.note: A patch-infrastructure foothold — independent of Kerberos entirely, so it survives a krbtgt double-reset that kills the ticket mechanisms.

steps.label: DnsAdmins ServerLevelPluginDll (DC SYSTEM via a DLL)
steps.note: Load a plugin DLL into the DNS service running as SYSTEM on the DC — a separate write-privesc persistence lever, gated on a control path over the DC/DnsAdmins.

steps.label: SID-history injection (cross-forest / hidden DA membership)
steps.note: Inject a high-privilege SID into an account you control — persistence that does not depend on holding krbtgt, and reaches across a trust when one exists.
